decision: Reject the bounded owned-text cache candidate; restore the published runtime unchanged.
candidate: Eight mixed-index slots, weak dictionary identity, separately admitted string owners, retained hit handles, optional insertion after successful comparisons, workspace-before-cache reclamation propagated across ancestors.
findings: All six real query cases slowed in both comparisons despite predicted decode reuse.
Overall admitted peaks were identical to the baseline in every case; temporary key retention did not improve whole-query peaks.
Successful lifetime/admission tests and simulated hit rates do not establish a worthwhile optimization.
The experiment does not isolate which ownership/cache operations dominate elapsed time; no causal allocation-profile claim is made.
reproduce: Check out baseline 1cb0dcb in an isolated checkout and apply the archived patch.
scope: Alternating fresh Node processes, six independent DuckDB Parquet cases, one warmup/four measured pairs in each run, full result parity and zero cleanup checks. No cloud-throughput or total-runtime cap claim.
remaining: Preserve measured same-entry comparison reuse and direct access as the current default.
Any further cross-comparison reuse needs substantially lower management cost and fresh end-to-end evidence.
F5 broader acceptance, JSON row-kernel performance and complete memory/runtime audit remain open.
